Novovorontsovka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kherson Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. None of the locals interviewed had ever heard of a Jewish cemetery in Novovorontsovka itself; they instead recalled that a flood around 1950 to 1953 submerged several villages and half of the town, suggesting any historical cemetery here may now lie underwater. The available Jewish cemetery evidence instead comes from the nearby colony of Vysokopillya (known as Kronau until 1915), founded in 1869 as a Lutheran German agricultural colony that Jews joined in the 1870s; a 1994–95 survey found evidence of Jewish burials, possibly a distinct section, within that colony's German cemetery, though only a small part of it survives today with no identifiable Jewish graves. It remains unknown whether the Jews of this area ever had a separate cemetery of their own.
